screws.min_engagement.measured_on: decided, with one measured case behind the M3 value: the face threads of a bought motor are 4.5 deep, the stock length that fits engages 3.4 and the next one bottoms, so 3.2 is the strictest M3 minimum that a real stack reaches with stock lengths. Four values were in use for M3: 3.0 (a length generator), 3.2 (a report), 4 (the whole insert) and 4 to 5 (a rule text); 2.4 was called too little. 4 to 5 cannot be reached in a 4.0 mm insert, 4 fails the measured motor thread, 3.0 is looser: all three are superseded. Other sizes: about one thread diameter, not measured
screws.min_engagement.description: threaded length of a screw inside its insert, nut or tapped part, per thread size
screws.min_engagement.x_note: The one definition of the engagement minimum. rules/tables/screws.json points here and holds no second number.

screws.min_under_head.measured_on: owner decision of one project after a printed 2 mm retainer left about 0.1 mm under countersunk heads; not a measured limit
screws.min_under_head.description: plastic that stays under a screw head, along the screw

screws.tip_room_min.measured_on: decided after an M3x12 bottomed in a 6 mm pocket; not measured
screws.tip_room_min.description: free length between the screw tip and the end of its hole or thread

screws.ref_pattern.measured_on: decided, not measured: the words screw and bolt, and a thread with a length as a screw is named (M3x12, M2.5 x 6; a third number, as in a washer M3x12x1.5 or an insert M3x4x5, is no screw). Set it to how screw refs are named. A ref the pattern does not match is not checked by the screw rules; hardware.recognised says so when it sits in a screw hole
screws.ref_pattern.description: a body whose name (or whose component's name) matches is a candidate for a screw; its shape decides: a head on a shank of a table thread, or a set screw when its own name says so

screws.any_hole_d_max.measured_on: decided, nobody measured it: the coarse clearance hole of an M12 screw (ISO 273). The screws table ends at M6; a project that bolts with larger screws sets it
screws.any_hole_d_max.description: the widest hole or slot of no table that counts as one a screw could use, when the gate decides whether a question about screws can apply to a part. A part with such a hole is asked; it is never taken for a part without screws

screws.head_recess_min.measured_on: owner decision of one project: a head sits just below the face; not a measured limit
screws.head_recess_min.description: least depth of a head below the face of its counterbore

screws.head_recess_max.measured_on: owner decision of one project after counterbores 7 to 15 mm deep left 2 to 3.6 mm under the heads; not a measured limit
screws.head_recess_max.description: a head sits no deeper than this below the face: the thread is reached by the screw length

screws.min_count_load_joint.measured_on: owner decision of one project after a base joint carried its torque on 2 screws; not computed for another load
screws.min_count_load_joint.description: least number of screws on a joint that carries torque or tipping

screws.hole_overcut.measured_on: decided after a hole cut to a typed depth was closed by a 0.84 mm cap when the body grew
screws.hole_overcut.description: a screw hole is cut this far past the face it must open on

screws.clamp_screws_off_axis_min.measured_on: decided after a printed two-piece cam slipped on its one screw
screws.clamp_screws_off_axis_min.description: least number of screws, off the axis, of a friction clamp on a rotation axis

screws.air_gap_max.measured_on: decided: the gap a local pad was given after a printed shell with a 0.35 gap cracked at its seam screws
screws.air_gap_max.description: air between two parts along a screw that clamps them

screws.bridge_search_r.measured_on: decided, not measured: a clamp screw stands next to the ring it closes on, about the radius of a large washer away. A flange that reaches farther than this over an open gap bends before it clamps
screws.bridge_search_r.description: how far from the axis of a screw a bought body may stand in the air gap between two clamped parts and still count as what the screw closes on (a bearing ring the two parts clamp between them)

screws.local_wall_min.measured_on: decided for the reprint of a shell whose 1.5 mm skirt cracked at its screws; not measured further
screws.local_wall_min.description: wall of a thin shell where a screw goes through it

screws.family.default: hex socket: cap DIN 912, button ISO 7380, countersunk DIN 7991
screws.family.measured_on: the family one project standardised on; a project names its own
screws.family.description: the one screw family and drive of a project

screws.insert_torque.default: 0.25 to 0.3 N*m for M3 into a brass insert, never over 0.4
screws.insert_torque.measured_on: decided from general practice, not measured on a print
screws.insert_torque.description: tightening torque written into the assembly notes for a screw into a heat-set insert

screws.solid_shank_max.measured_on: decided: the resolution of the probe (it follows the shank in 0.25 mm steps and refines an end to 0.02). A tip that only touches the end of its hole is screws.tip_bottoming
screws.solid_shank_max.description: length of a screw shank that may lie in solid printed plastic before its hole counts as closed

screws.nut_ref_pattern.measured_on: naming habit of one project; set it to how nut refs are named
screws.nut_ref_pattern.description: a ref body whose name matches is a nut: a thread a screw may end in

rules.title: A screw reaches far enough into its thread
rules.statement: Every screw is engaged over at least {screws.min_engagement} (per thread size) in its insert, nut or tapped part. Its length comes from the stack: plastic under the head, the parts between, the engagement, ending short of the hole end. A change of length moves everything stacked on the screw: length and seat change together. A screw whose thread nothing receives (no insert, no nut, no hole narrower than the thread anywhere along it) is a finding with 0 mm: the row names the hole and the part its thread ends in and what lies on that axis.
rules.why: Screws with 2.4 mm of engagement were found in a finished model, and six refs were named 2 to 6 mm shorter than the screw the stack needed. Four different minimums were in use and none of them stopped an export.
fix_order: Shorten the stack under the head.
Never reach the thread by a deeper counterbore.
Nothing receives the thread: model the insert or nut as a ref body, or name the body that is there so that its ref pattern matches.
rules.note: 0 mm with nothing on the axis is FAIL, not NOT_RUN: the screw unit follows the whole thread and counts any solid body round it, named or not, so nothing found is a measurement of the model as drawn. A thread that exists only in the real bought part (a tapped housing drawn without its holes) is the owner's waiver with that reason.

rules.title: Plastic under every screw head
rules.statement: Under every screw head at least {screws.min_under_head} of plastic stays, measured along the screw. A plate too thin for it is made thicker; neighbours of the project's own design move before the plate is thinned. A head that bears through its washer on a bought rigid body and on no plastic (a clamp washer on a bearing ring, within {washers.landing_gap_max}) crushes no plastic: it is judged as a clamp, not here.
rules.why: A printed 2 mm retainer left about 0.1 mm under countersunk heads and was deleted. Deep counterbores left 2 to 3.6 mm under other heads.
fix_order: Use a shallower head recess and a longer stock screw.
A head that must stay deep because the space above it is swept: an owner waiver with the reason.
rules.note: The washer decides: its landing on a bearing ring, or a hardware body as the first thing under it in contact (no second washer, and no insert, nut or screw by its name: those sit in plastic), with no printed body in contact. A washer that lies on plastic, also beside a ring, leaves the screw under this rule; so does a washer whose covers the facts do not list. washers.landing and bearings.clamp_room judge the clamp itself.

rules.title: A screw does not bottom
rules.statement: The tip of every screw stops at least {screws.tip_room_min} before the end of its hole, pocket or bought thread.
rules.why: An M3x12 bottomed in a 6 mm pocket and the joint stayed loose. In a 4.5 mm motor face thread the next stock length after the one that fits bottoms.
fix_order: Pick the next shorter stock length.
Deepen the tip hole below the insert.

rules.title: One screw family, in stock lengths
rules.statement: A project uses one screw family and drive ({screws.family}) in the lengths its owner stocks (rules/tables/screws.json, stock_lengths). The length that reaches the thread is chosen; no long through-bolts. A length outside the stock list is flagged before the design depends on it.
rules.why: Twelve parts had short screws at the bottom of 7 to 15 mm deep counterbores because only three lengths were allowed, and all were exported again once longer screws were bought. Later a length outside the agreed list was designed in twice.

attest.question: Is every screw of this part of the project family and of a length in the stock list?
labels: every screw of this part is of the project family and a stock length
some are not: listed in the report for the owner

rules.note: Deferred: no judge yet. The facts are there: the screw probe reads size and length of every screw ref.
supersedes: only three short lengths, with a deep counterbore instead

rules.title: A counterbore is only as deep as the head
rules.statement: A counterbore is the head height plus {screws.head_recess_min} to {screws.head_recess_max}. The thread is reached by the screw length, never by a deep counterbore. A head is not raised into a zone that a moving part sweeps.
rules.why: Deep counterbores left 2 to 3.6 mm of plastic under the heads, and one part kept 18.6 mm deep counterbores against the rule.
fix_order: Use the next longer stock screw and a shallower counterbore.
Fill under the head rather than leaving it proud or deep.

attest.question: Does every head of this part sit between the two recess limits?
labels: every head sits within the recess limits
some heads sit deeper because raising them would enter a swept zone: listed in the report for the owner
this part has no screw heads

rules.note: Deferred: no judge yet. The facts are there: the screw probe reads the recess of every head seat. screws.under_head already stops the worst case, a counterbore that eats the plastic under the head.

rules.title: Enough screws on a joint that carries load
rules.statement: A joint that carries torque or tipping has at least {screws.min_count_load_joint} screws, on the largest bolt circle the parts allow; the count comes from the load on the farthest screw. A clamp plate in the load path keeps its thickness and its screw count: neighbours of the project's own design move before the plate is thinned or a screw is dropped.
rules.why: A strip carried the whole torque of a base joint on 2 screws. A six-screw flange on a small circle came out at a safety factor of 3.5 to 4, and one part was printed with it. Two clamp plates were 8.5 and 6.7 mm thick on four button heads because the block under them was low.

attest.question: Does this part sit in a joint that carries torque or tipping, and how many screws hold it?
labels: no joint of this part carries torque or tipping
every load joint of this part has at least the minimum count, on the largest circle the parts allow
fewer: listed in the report for the owner

auto.na: this part has no screw, no screw hole and no insert pocket: no screw holds it

rules.note: Asked once per changed part. The load per screw is not computed: the count is the answer, and "fewer" goes to the owner in the report.

rules.title: A head bears on a full ring
rules.statement: A head bears on a full ring of plastic: hole and seat lie fully inside material, with a margin to the edge. A counterbore near an edge becomes a U-slot or gets a boss. Heads of neighbouring screws do not overlap, and no screw ends in air.
rules.why: Heads bore half on plastic over the corner of a motor body, two screws sat half outside their tab, and a bracket had intersecting heads. All were found in models.

attest.question: Does every head of this part bear on a full ring of plastic?
labels: every head bears on a full ring
some heads sit in a U-slot on purpose and bear on both flanks: listed in the report for the owner
this part has no screw heads

rules.note: Deferred: no judge yet. The facts are there: the screw probe reads the share of each head seat that lies on material.

rules.title: A screw clamps plastic, not air
rules.statement: A screw never clamps across an air gap through a thin wall. A local pad closes the gap to {screws.air_gap_max} so the screw clamps plastic in compression, and the wall round the screw is at least {screws.local_wall_min}. The open gap of a bearing clamp is the one exception: there the screw closes on the ring. That holds for a clamp washer on a ring, and for a gap between two parts that a bought solid body bridges (a bearing ring the parts clamp between them): it stands in the gap within {screws.bridge_search_r} of the screw axis and both parts press on it along the screw, each within {bearings.contact_gap_max}. A gap with nothing in it stays a finding, and so does a body that only one part presses on: a ring in a bore with no shoulder behind it, a pin through both parts, a part that stops short of the body.
rules.why: A printed shell with a 1.5 mm skirt and a 0.35 mm gap cracked at its six seam screws and was printed again with pads.
fix_order: Add a local pad that closes the gap, so the screw clamps plastic in compression.
Thicken the wall round the screw.
A gap that is the clamp room of a ring: model the ring as a bought body in the gap, with both parts landing on it; the screw unit then finds it.
A gap that must stay open: owner waiver that names the screw and what it closes on.
rules.note: The air gap is measured along every screw whose head is on the part. The screw of a clamp washer on a bearing ring is left out (bearings.clamp_room). What stands in a gap is read by the screw unit ("gaps" of a screw: the two bodies either side, and the bought bodies in the gap, each with the air between it and either part on one line parallel to the screw). A gap that a bought body bridges is one INFO row per part that names the body, so the exception can be checked by eye; the ring itself is judged by the bearing rules. The screws of one part across a gap with the same body in it that does not bridge it are one row: one cause, one decision. Facts of an older unit hold no "gaps": the finding stays as it was and says to collect the facts again. The wall round the screw (screws.local_wall_min) is not measured yet: text only.

rules.title: The whole screw path is open
rules.statement: For every screw the path head seat, clearance hole, thread is open: no more than {screws.solid_shank_max} of the shank lies in solid printed plastic. Holes are cut through-all or {screws.hole_overcut} past the face, never to a typed depth that a later growth of the body can close. Holes and pockets are checked again after every join or fill. One skin is meant: the sacrificial bridge right under a head whose counterbore prints facing the bed, up to one bridge step ({overhang.bridge_step}) thick. It is told with its bench step and does not fail here; whether it is a bridge layer or a leftover skin is asked once, by access.hole_closed. The same skin anywhere else along the screw fails.
rules.why: One printed part had a screw hole closed by a 0.84 mm cap, another had its clamp screws blocked by a 1.5 mm wall in front of the inserts. Both were drilled by hand.
fix_order: Cut the hole again through everything the screw passes, through-all or past the face.
Find the join or fill that closed it and move it down the timeline, or cut after it.
rules.note: Judged from the screw refs: the core of the shank inside a printed body is a closed hole, whatever the thickness of the fill. A cap in front of a hole with no screw ref in it is access.hole_closed; a screw into a pilot hole in the plastic is inserts.no_tapped_plastic.

rules.title: A friction clamp needs two screws or a shape lock
rules.statement: A friction clamp on a rotation axis has at least {screws.clamp_screws_off_axis_min} screws off the axis, or a shape lock: flats, a key, teeth. A clamp longer than one screw pitch has screws along its length. A slit clamp is slit through everything that would hold it open. An adjusting screw whose load reverses is captured both ways.
rules.why: A printed clamp could not be closed onto its motor because the slit was bridged, and was sawn open. A printed two-piece cam slipped on its one screw.

rules.title: Torque and thread locker are written down
rules.statement: The assembly notes give a torque for screws into inserts: {screws.insert_torque}. Clamp screws get low-strength thread locker. No anaerobic locker on a screw threaded into printed plastic. Under heads on nylon use a washer or a wide head and tighten again after the first days: the plastic creeps.
rules.why: No single failed print behind it: screws into inserts were tightened by feel, and nylon under a head relaxes.

rules.title: The thread of a bought part is read, not assumed
rules.statement: The thread size of a bought part is read from its model and measured on the part (a D4.0 hole means M4), never assumed. Clearance hole and counterbore then come from the table row of that size.
rules.why: A printed box had M3 holes and counterbores for a power supply with M4 threads and was drilled out by hand.

rules.title: Stacked parts share one screw set
rules.statement: Parts that lie in series on one bolt circle share one screw set: the screw goes through all of them into the inserts of the last part, its head on the outer part with at least {screws.min_under_head} under it, in a stock length. The parts stay separate. Before adding inserts for a new part, look for a screw set that already passes there.
rules.why: Two parts in series each had their own ring of screws and inserts: 16 screws and 18 inserts that added parts, not strength, because the weaker ring still carried everything. One shared set made it 8 and 8.
rules.note: What it can cost, to name when it is used: coarser indexing between the parts, and a head that ends up under a part fitted later (access.head_under_later_part).
